learning_objective: 🎯 Explore the fragile world of adolescent fantasy, hero worship, and the painful collision between wild teenage dreams and harsh socio-economic realities.

main_concepts.simple_explanation: Sophie is a teenager from a lower-middle-class family who dreams of owning the best boutique in the city, becoming a manager, an actress, or a fashion designer. She constantly lives in a dream world.
Jansie is Sophie's practical and realistic friend. She knows they are both earmarked to work in the local biscuit factory and tries to bring Sophie down to earth, but Sophie refuses to listen.
Geoff is Sophie's older brother, an apprentice mechanic who speaks very little. Sophie is fascinated by his silence and imagines he has access to exotic, unknown worlds that she wishes to enter.
Sophie fabricates a story that she met Danny Casey, a famous Irish football prodigy, at a clothing store (Royce's). She lies to Geoff that Casey promised to meet her again for a date.

Sophie goes to the canal to wait for Casey. Even though she made the whole story up, she gets so absorbed in her own lie that she genuinely waits for him, feels the pangs of doubt, and walks back home burdened by immense sadness.

fun_activity.title: 💭 The Reality Check
fun_activity.instructions: Sophie dreams of being a boutique owner while destined for a biscuit factory. What is your wildest, most impossible dream job? Write it down, and then write down the very first realistic step you need to take toward it.

exam_tips: 📌 Contrast Sophie and Jansie: Sophie is an escapist and a romantic dreamer who ignores reality. Jansie is grounded, practical, and accepts her socio-economic limitations.
📌 Understand Sophie's relationship with Geoff: She tells him the Danny Casey lie because she craves his attention and wants to be part of his mysterious, silent world.
📌 The title 'Going Places' is highly ironic. Sophie is physically going nowhere (stuck in her poor town), but mentally, she travels to glamorous places and meets famous athletes.
quick_recap: ⭐ Sophie's father represents the harsh, unromantic reality. He dismisses her Danny Casey story immediately as another one of her 'wild stories'.
⭐ Danny Casey was a real player for United, but the meeting at the arcade was purely a figment of Sophie's imagination.
⭐ The burden of the lie crushes Sophie at the end, as she has to live with the self-inflicted pain of a broken 'promise'.
